_note: The Astrology lens: planet → god-image → archetype → corpus quotes. Quotations name only their work and words; `npm run astrology` places each in the read-only corpus (scripts/lib/cite.mjs) and fails on any it cannot place once. The field ties per body (and their Jung quotes, basis jung / inferred / site) come from curation/sky/ties.json, and Burt's planet quotes from curation/sky/burt.json, both already verified by `npm run sky:check`. Lines are mine: they say only what the quotes under them show. Outer planets: Jung's sources stop at Saturn; for Uranus, Neptune and Pluto the reading is Burt's, and the lens says so.

frame.quote: The planetary names refer ultimately not only to metals but, as every alchemist knew, to the (astrological) temperaments, that is, to psychic factors.
the journey through the planetary houses boils down to becoming conscious of the good and the bad qualities in our character, and the apotheosis means no more than maximum consciousness
The horoscope (fig. 100) is itself a mandala (a clock) with a dark centre

pillars.quote: The positions of sun, moon, and ascendant form the three main pillars of the horoscope.

order.line: The walk climbs the planetary ladder, Moon to Saturn, past the three planets Jung's sources did not know, and ends at the Sun. That is where the old ascent ended too.

saturn.line: Lead, the old king, the dark sun: the heaviest of the seven and the one the alchemists conjured as a familiar.

quotes.quote: is none other than the leaden spirit or planetary demon Saturn
When, therefore, an alchemist conjured up the spirit of Saturn as his familiar, this was an attempt to bring to consciousness a standpoint outside the ego

uranus.name: Uranus
uranus.line: Found in 1781. Jung's sources never knew it; the reading here is Burt's.

neptune.name: Neptune
neptune.line: Found in 1846. Jung's sources never knew it; the reading here is Burt's.

pluto.name: Pluto
pluto.line: Found in 1930. Jung's sources never knew it; the reading here is Burt's.

sun.name: Sun
sun.line: Gold, the end of the ascent. Every chart has a Sun, and Jung reads the sun as a symbol of the self. That is the link every walk ends on.

people.label: C. G. Jung
people.line: Jung is the first chart here. The corpus gives the year and the region; the day and the village come from the public record. It gives no birth time, so his chart is cast for local noon: no rising sign, and the Moon may be a few degrees off.
